headline_marked: Police HQ clarify [[IGP's 'crossfire' remark]], deny extrajudicial killings
headline: Police HQ clarify IGP's 'crossfire' remark, deny extrajudicial killings
summary: Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir sparked backlash after saying police are ready for 'crossfire' if the government permits.
details: Police Headquarters clarified on Monday that Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir did not mean extrajudicial killings when he used the term 'crossfire' during a discussion on law and order.
The clarification came after political parties and organizations criticized the IGP's remarks, made at the opening of the Community Islamic Bank System in Dhaka's Chawkbazar.
During the event, the IGP stated, 'If crossfire is needed and the government allows it, we will do that,' prompting demands for the withdrawal of the statement.
In response, Police Headquarters stated that the IGP was expressing his commitment to taking effective action against drug traders, terrorists, and criminals threatening public safety.
The headquarters further explained that the term 'crossfire' was used in its literal sense to convey firmness in law enforcement and not as a reference to punishment outside the judicial process.
The statement also highlighted that police officers have faced 176 attacks in the first 10 months of this year, resulting in four deaths and 370 serious injuries.
Police cited the Penal Code 1860, Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, and Police Act 1861 as laws that recognize the right to self-defence for police officers.
Additionally, the IGP expressed frustration with journalists' criticism, stating that police are called 'fascist' when using batons and 'weak' if they remain silent.
Police Headquarters later clarified that the IGP's comments regarding journalists were inadvertent and not intended as sweeping statements.
caption:
The IGP said police are ready for 'crossfire' if the government permits. Now, Police HQ is scrambling to clarify.

Police Headquarters clarified on Monday that Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir did not mean extrajudicial killings when he used the term 'crossfire' during a discussion on law and order.

The clarification came after political parties and organizations criticized the IGP's remarks, made at the opening of the Community Islamic Bank System in Dhaka's Chawkbazar.

During the event, the IGP stated, 'If crossfire is needed and the government allows it, we will do that,' prompting demands for the withdrawal of the statement.

In response, Police Headquarters stated that the IGP was expressing his commitment to taking effective action against drug traders, terrorists, and criminals threatening public safety.

The headquarters further explained that the term 'crossfire' was used in its literal sense to convey firmness in law enforcement and not as a reference to punishment outside the judicial process.

The statement also highlighted that police officers have faced 176 attacks in the first 10 months of this year, resulting in four deaths and 370 serious injuries.

Police cited the Penal Code 1860, Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, and Police Act 1861 as laws that recognize the right to self-defence for police officers.

Additionally, the IGP expressed frustration with journalists' criticism, stating that police are called 'fascist' when using batons and 'weak' if they remain silent.

Police Headquarters later clarified that the IGP's comments regarding journalists were inadvertent and not intended as sweeping statements.

headline: Cyclone Arnab forms over Bay, ports hoist signal 2
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) reports the system has intensified into a cyclone and is moving west-northwestwards.
details: A deep depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal has intensified and developed into Cyclone Arnab, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).
The storm is currently located over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay, with maximum sustained wind speeds of about 62kmph, rising to 88kmph in gusts.
The BMD has advised the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No. 2.
The cyclone is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by midnight on Monday.
It is further predicted to become a very severe cyclonic storm and cross India’s Andhra coast on Wednesday.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.
The name 'Arnab', meaning sea or ocean, was proposed by Bangladesh as part of a regional naming process involving 13 countries.
caption:
Cyclone Arnab has formed in the Bay of Bengal. Warning signal 2 has been issued for four maritime ports.

A deep depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal has intensified and developed into Cyclone Arnab, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).

The BMD has advised the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No. 2.

The cyclone is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by midnight on Monday.

It is further predicted to become a very severe cyclonic storm and cross India’s Andhra coast on Wednesday.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.
